rows.text: calls `0020E600(dword [rcx])` and, when that is non-null, calls `0020E600(dword [rcx])` again and stores `dx` at word `rcx+0x60` when byte `+0x6` of the second result is non-zero; a null first result or a zero byte returns without writing

calls `0020E600(dword [rcx])` and scans byte `rcx+4` entries of 0x30 bytes starting at the result plus 0x2A, returning the index of the first entry whose word shifted right by 4 equals `edx`, or 0xFFF when none matches or the count is 0

clears bits 6 and 7 of byte `rcx+9`; when `edx` is 0 it then sets bit 0x40 of that byte and zeroes byte `+0x8`; otherwise, when byte `+0x9` has any of bits 0x30 set, it clears bit 0x20 and sets bit 0x10, and when the result is below 0x40 and byte `+0x8` is 0 it stores qword 8 at `+0x10`, word 1 at `+0xA` and byte 1 at `+0x8`; the other paths return without further writes

notes: 0040DB00 is also entered from `003E1210` + 0x5B; it does not test the 0020E600 result for null. 00471B20: the 'below 0x40' test at 00471B37 always passes because the entry instruction cleared bits 6 and 7; the sentence states the instruction as written.
